items.title: 12.9 Stability of the oxidation states of sulfur

source_refs.note: Topic 12.9 with Figure 12.9 and Quick Check 12.4, printed pages 281-282.

blocks.text: The Stability of oxidation states of sulphur is explained by Frost diagram in which an element X is a plot of nE⁰ vs oxidation state (n) for the redox couple X(n)/X(0) as shown in Figure 12.9. It tells about the relative stabilities of different oxidation states of an element at two extreme pH values (pH=0 and pH=14) i.e. acidic and basic conditions. It can also be regarded as a plot between standard reaction Gibb’s free energy (∆G°) versus oxidation state (n) because oxidation state(n) is directly proportional to ∆G° as shown below.
Here E⁰ is the standard reduction potential, F is the Faraday constant and n is the number of transferred electrons in a redox half reaction.

The more stable oxidation state has a lower nE⁰ value or more negative Gibb’s free energy. Therefore, the more stable oxidation state is at the lowest position in the diagram. Further, a couple with a more positive slope is a good oxidising agent, while a couple with a more negative slope is a good reducing agent.

blocks.alt: Frost diagram: nE° (V) from −5 to 2 on the vertical axis against oxidation state (n) −II, 0, II, IV, VI. Black dotted line, acidic solution: H2S(g) at about −0.35, S8 at 0, SO2(aq) at about 1.8 and SO4 2− at about 2.25. Blue dotted line, basic solution: S2− at about 0.8, S8 at 0, SO3 2− at about −2.6 and SO4 2− at about −4.6.
blocks.caption: Figure 12.9: Frost diagram for oxidation states of sulfur (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 12.9).

blocks.text: In the diagram for sulfur, +6 (SO₄²⁻) is the most thermodynamically stable oxidation state, completely non-oxidising under extreme basic conditions, while under extreme acidic conditions, it is shown to be very unstable.

It can be seen that in basic environments, the oxidized sulfur states are all more stable than the elemental form but under acidic conditions all the oxidized sulfur states are less stable than the elemental form.

blocks.title: Quick Check 12.4
blocks.text:
a) Determine the oxidation state of S in the following species.
i. SO₃
ii. H₂SO₄
iii. SO₄²⁻
iv. S₂O₃²⁻
b) Which oxidation states of sulphur are the most common? Explain your answer with reason.
c) Explain the involvement of d orbital in variable oxidation states of S in its compounds.
